observation: Synthetic pilot reports split between easier sleep onset and increased alertness after brief self-hypnosis immediately before bed. The difference may depend on induction style, prior experience, and whether the session ends with energizing language.
contexts: Three people were new to self-hypnosis.
Two used a session containing an alertness-oriented return.
confounders: Caffeine timing changed for one contributor.
Baseline insomnia severity was not measured consistently.
adverseSignals: One contributor reported feeling more mentally activated for approximately an hour.
One reported benefit on the first night but poorer sleep on the second night.
unknowns: The reports are synthetic examples, not participant evidence.
It is unknown whether route language or timing explains the split.
External evidence has not been checked.
